How is this sentient?

From the article:

In approximately 50% of cases where a volunteer was not able to identify a locking device as such, SCP-005 was not successful in deactivating the device. Due to these results, SCP-005 has been tentatively classified as 'sentient' and further tests are being run to determine its cognitive abilities.

item.title: Happy Holidays, Zyn!
item.content:encoded:
Home, is where I want to be
But I guess I'm already there
I come home, she lifted up her wings
I guess that this must be the place


~David Byrne, "This Must Be the Place"

This tale is my attempt at emulating the style of Zyn's original Kiryu Labs series — probably one of the best early series on this site, propped up by Zyn's talent for writing heartwarming, touching stories with just the right balance between humour and heartfelt emotion. I hope I did Kiryu Labs justice with this.

Thanks to VoidLady, not_a_seagull, and Its a Bad Idea for helping me revise and edit this tale, and special thanks to Zyn for all that she does to help this community thrive. Have a wonderful New Year.

Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

Moved to Ideas Critique since there's no draft here.

Also noting that this:

An scp that knows everything there is know about the foundation, it's object class is: Thaumiel so it must be helpful? Well yes (sometimes) but mostly no, it hates almost everyone in foundation

Doesn't make sense for a Thaumiel anomaly. If it's not a reliable form of containment, it shouldn't be Thaumiel. Doesn't matter how overpowered and intelligent it is; if the Foundation can't trust it, they won't use it. Moving forward, I suggest reading over this essay on common SCP pitfalls to get an idea of what elements to avoid putting in an SCP article.

item.title: Re: Scp idea
item.content:encoded:
Hi there!
So, first things first: this is way too vague and short to make an in-depth evaluation. You have used not even half of the 400 words limit, so my suggestion is to start fleshing out this idea right here right now. This will make futurw critiques more accurate and helpful.
As a second note, I also suggest investing on the narrative. The format "this is a thing that makes things" was good enough for the first series but now the community want a story rather than a thing that makes things.
In the case of your idea, you can explore this SCP's hatred towards the Foundation, what has it done to warrant it? What has the SCP done against them? How does it get information? Does it know only known facts or can it tell unknown information about the other anomalies? You didn't even tell if the SCP is a human, an animal, a machine or whatever.
This is not a bad idea per se but you have a long way to develop it. Wish you success!


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique

item.title: Author post!
item.content:encoded:
How do you write about an infectious disease in a global pandemic? Apparently you just have to make it cute!

I had a lot of fun writing this SCiP for Rigen for the holiday exchange! When I first got the prompt of making “art or tale about anomalous disease SCP/SCPs" I was really unsure of what to do since I couldn't figure out a way to do a tale about a disease without paralleling the current pandemic (and I honestly didn't realize that the request was for art or tale rather than an SCP until like 2 days before the due date). But I think what came out is fun and people have said it’s funny, cute, and really clever so I guess others agree! Happy Holidays everyone!
